The election took place concurrently with the [[2022 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|regularly scheduled election]] for Oklahoma's [[Classes of United States senators|other Senate seat]].{{cite news |last1=Beavers |first1=Olivia |last2=Everett |first2=Burgess |title=Inhofe to retire from Senate, teeing up special election in Oklahoma |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2022/02/24/inhofe-to-retire-from-senate-teeing-up-special-election-in-oklahoma-00011534 |access-date=February 25, 2022 |publisher=Politico |date=February 24, 2022}} The candidate filing deadline was between April 13 and 15, 2022. This special election was held to fill the remaining four years of incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Senator [[Jim Inhofe]]'s term. In February 2022, Inhofe announced that he would resign early at the end of the [[117th United States Congress]] on January 3, 2023, reportedly due to [[long COVID]].{{Cite magazine |last1=Otten |first1=Tori |last2=Thakker |first2=Prem |date=February 24, 2023 |title=The Ticker |url=https://newrepublic.com/post/170783/jim-inhofe-retired-due-long-covid-says-least-5-congressmembers-have-it |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240710052608/https://newrepublic.com/post/170783/jim-inhofe-retired-due-long-covid-says-least-5-congressmembers-have-it |archive-date=July }}{{Dead link|date=July 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Former [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Kendra Horn]] secured the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nomination by default, while the primary election for the [[Republican Party of Oklahoma|Republican]] nomination took place on June 28, 2022. U.S. Representative [[Markwayne Mullin]] won the Republican primary runoff on August 23, defeating former [[Oklahoma House of Representatives|State House]] Speaker [[T. W. Shannon]].{{cite web |title=2022 Statutory Election Dates and Deadlines |url=https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/elections/dates-and-deadlines/2022-statutory-dates-deadlines.pdf |website=oklahoma.gov |publisher=Oklahoma State Election Board |access-date=October 13, 2021 |archive-date=April 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220425080130/https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/elections/dates-and-deadlines/2022-statutory-dates-deadlines.pdf |url-status=dead }} Mullin ultimately won the election.{{Cite web |author=KOCO Staff |date=November 9, 2022 |title=Oklahoma Election Results: Markwayne Mullin wins race for US Senate, claiming Inhofe's open seat |url=https://www.koco.com/article/oklahoma-election-results-markwayne-mullin-wins-us-senate-race-kendra-horn/41780490 |access-date=November 9, 2022 |website=KOCO |language=en}} Mullin, a member of the [[Cherokee Nation]], became the first [[List of Native Americans in the United States Congress|Native American]] to serve in the U.S. Senate since fellow Republican [[Ben Nighthorse Campbell]] retired from Congress in 2005, and the first Native American representing this state since [[Robert Latham Owen|Robert Owen]] in 1925.{{Cite web |agency=Associated Press |title=Markwayne Mullin wins US Senate seat |url=https://indiancountrytoday.com/news/markwayne-mullin-wins-us-senate-seat |access-date=November 12, 2022 |website=ICT |language=en}} Conversely, Horn won [[Oklahoma County, Oklahoma|Oklahoma County]], making her the first Democrat since [[2008 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|2008]] to carry any Oklahoma county in a Senate election. == Republican primary == On February 25, 2022, [[Jim Inhofe]], the state's longest-serving U.S. senator, announced he would leave office at the end of the [[117th Congress]], triggering a special election for his U.S. Senate seat in [[Oklahoma]].{{cite news |last1=Eger |first1=Andrea |title=U.S. Sen. Jim Inhofe announces retirement after 35 years in Congress representing Oklahoma |url=https://tulsaworld.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/u-s-sen-jim-inhofe-announces-retirement-after-35-years-in-congress-representing-oklahoma/article_5e5c9fe0-9659-11ec-a498-dbc0862714df.html |access-date=February 25, 2022 |publisher=Tulsa World |date=February 25, 2022}} A crowded field of candidates was expected in the Republican primary following the announcement of his retirement.{{cite news |last1=Gorman |first1=Reese |title=Contenders for Oklahoma's open Senate seat face a crowded race |url=https://www.readfrontier.org/stories/contenders-for-oklahomas-open-senate-seat-face-a-crowded-race/ |access-date=February 25, 2022 |publisher=The Frontier |date=February 25, 2022}} Luke Holland, Inhofe's former chief of staff, launched his campaign for Inhofe's seat on the same day with Inhofe's endorsement. The next day, [[Markwayne Mullin]], a U.S. representative for [[Oklahoma's 2nd congressional district]], announced his campaign. By February 28, Oklahoma State Senator [[Nathan Dahm]] had announced he was switching his campaign from [[2022 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|running for Oklahoma's Class III seat]] to running for the special election seat. On March 8, former [[United States National Security Council]] chief of staff Alex Gray announced his campaign.{{cite news |last1=Vakil |first1=Caroline |title=Former Trump national security official jumps into Senate race in Oklahoma |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/597376-former-trump-national-security-official-jumps-into-senate-race-in-oklahoma |access-date=March 8, 2022 |work=The Hill |date=March 8, 2022}} [[T. W. Shannon]], a former [[speaker of the Oklahoma House of Representatives]], officially announced his campaign on March 11.
